architecture_decisions: The architecture decision is to implement a structured autonomous failure mechanism for exact repository-consent failure, retain current status semantics but return a bounded structured code without message parsing.
work_items: Implement a typed read-only provider operation that returns only one of: missing/unauthorized failure; commit-bearing repository with canonical default branch and head revision; positively empty repository with canonical default branch and no head revision. The operation uses existing exact-repository credential authority and returns no source bytes. Ordinary commit-bearing public/Python/.NET bootstrap remains unchanged.
validations: Validate the implementation by testing the structured autonomous failure mechanism with various scenarios, including exact repository-consent failure, missing/unauthorized failure, commit-bearing repository with canonical default branch and head revision, positively empty repository with canonical default branch and no head revision, and ordinary source failure alone cannot initialize greenfield lineage.
AC-01: validate protected requirement — Autonomy returns `REPOSITORY_AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED` as a bounded structured code without message parsing.
AC-02: validate protected requirement — Runtime introduces no PAT, reusable Vercel personal/team token, GitHub user token, password or static provider bearer to initiate repository consent.
AC-03: validate protected requirement — Preview is not granted production `github/parallax-runtime` mutation authority merely to make consent initiation testable.
AC-04: validate protected requirement — After external exact-repository consent, ordinary production Connect token exchange plus exact-one-repository GitHub verification remains the readiness proof.
AC-05: validate protected requirement — Permission changes preserve Project/work/run identity and the same Engineering Run remains retryable.
AC-06: validate protected requirement — Permission guidance appears only for exact authorization-required code; no unverified consent URL is surfaced.
AC-07: validate protected requirement — Typed read-only inspection deterministically distinguishes commit-bearing, positively empty and missing/unauthorized states under exact scope.
AC-08: validate protected requirement — Outage, 404/403, credential failure, malformed response or ordinary source failure alone cannot initialize greenfield lineage.
AC-09: validate protected requirement — Dedicated greenfield initialization creates a zero-file root with canonical empty digest/provenance; ordinary source packages remain non-empty.
AC-10: validate protected requirement — Zero-file manifest/materialization is accepted only for exact root-greenfield invariants; forged empty implementation/non-greenfield lineage is rejected.
AC-11: validate protected requirement — IMPLEMENT produces at least one safe protected file and changed non-root lineage before BUILD/TEST/VERIFY can pass.
AC-12: validate protected requirement — PLAN through VERIFY performs no GitHub source/ref mutation merely to initialize empty baseline.

AC-13: validate protected requirement — At REVIEW, fixed initializer creates the deterministic bootstrap root commit via repository-contents API, serially deletes the exact bootstrap file, and proves the resulting default-branch head tree is empty.

AC-14: validate protected requirement — Replay reuses an existing baseline only when cleanup head, bootstrap parent, parent count, trees, fixed path/content/messages/actor, provenance and default ref all match exactly.
AC-15: validate protected requirement — Any unrelated head, extra file, modified bootstrap or incompatible ref state fails closed and is never overwritten/force-updated.

AC-16: validate protected requirement — The bootstrap path is absent from the verified default-branch head before accepted implementation publication; it exists only in immutable initialization history.
AC-17: validate protected requirement — Accepted application source is committed on bounded Parallax branch from the verified empty baseline, never directly to default by the initializer.
AC-18: validate protected requirement — Existing PR create/read-back proves exact repository, head branch/revision and base branch.
AC-19: validate protected requirement — Vercel Preview is created from exact accepted commit and read-back proves repository/source revision/target identity.
AC-20: validate protected requirement — Delivery records bounded initialization, accepted commit, PR and Preview evidence without credentials/raw provider payloads and remains replay-safe.
AC-21: validate protected requirement — Commit-bearing public bootstrap, Python acceptance, OT Time .NET source-only acceptance, ordinary lineage and GitHub delivery remain green.
AC-22: validate protected requirement — Greenfield support does not add Vercel application-delivery dependency to source-only mode.
AC-23: validate protected requirement — Greenfield publication ends at REVIEW and cannot approve work, promote production or complete REVIEW.
AC-24: validate protected requirement — Runtime/provider/client code does not inspect Decision Ledger identity, `sickbeard`, benchmark tokens or expected solution content.

AC-25: validate protected requirement — Authorization probe/preview marker and temporary qualification/focused workflows are absent from final PR; negative capability evidence remains governance evidence only.

AC-26: validate protected requirement — Release record states workload-OIDC consent initiation was not proven and GitHub REST cannot create a ref in an empty repository; neither is represented as a deployed capability.

AC-27: validate protected requirement — After explicit exact-repository consent, canonical Decision Ledger trial proceeds without out-of-band source edits through positive empty proof, greenfield root, accepted source, protected BUILD/TEST/VERIFY, REVIEW-only REST baseline, bounded branch/PR, Vercel Preview and REVIEW.
AC-28: validate protected requirement — Any newly exposed consent/inspection/initialization/delivery/Preview boundary is recorded and separately governed rather than weakening gates.

AC-29: validate protected requirement — This amended exact spec obtains authentic DSPy SpecCritic + SpecCompiler evidence before provider/delivery semantic implementation. Final exact head passes protected spec validation, focused/full API tests, applicable client/browser acceptance, Bounded Autonomy, protected promotion and release gates before merge/deployment.
risks: The risk is to introduce a new type of failure that may not be easily detected or handled by the client, leading to potential data loss or security breaches.
